message.content: In lions, the most well‑known dominant genetic trait is the presence of a mane in adult males. The allele that codes for the mane’s development is dominant, so when a male lion inherits this allele from either parent, it will express the mane phenotype. This dominant trait is what gives male lions their characteristic mane, while females (who lack the dominant allele) do not develop one.
